title: Stochastic arg-fuzz eval harness for function selection precision
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: Build an automated, stochastic evaluation harness that detects regressions in function/tool selection accuracy and argument/schema validation after model, runtime, or config changes. This harness will exercise the tool-calling surface by generating randomized prompt variants, sampling model responses, performing schema fuzzing on arguments, and measuring selection precision, false positive invocations, and argument conformance. The output should be a reproducible daily job, per-commit checks for PRs touching routing/config, and a dashboard with drift alerts and example failures for triage.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs as a scheduled job in CI (daily) and as a pre-merge check for changes touching routing, model pinning, or invocation handlers.
Produces per-run metrics: top-1 selection accuracy, top-3 coverage, schema-conformance rate, argument-normalization-error-rate, and false-positive-invocation-rate.
Regression detection thresholds configurable per-model and per-route; when breached, generate an alert and attach representative failing prompts and responses.
Integration with eval-store so labeled ground-truth and historical runs can be compared; ability to rerun with fixed seeds for debuggability.
End-to-end tests exercising both 'clean' nominal cases and adversarial fuzzed argument shapes (missing fields, wrong types, shuffled keys) with expected pass/fail labels.
implementation_notes: Use existing eval-runner infra and extend with a new 'invocation_fuzz' job type that composes prompt templates with stochastic fillers from the prompt-corpus service.
Fuzzing: introduce a focused schema-fuzzer that mutates argument payloads (type flips, field drops, nested corruption) and measures parser/validator behavior in the tool adapters.
Scoring: canonicalize model outputs to a structured invocation event (tool_id, args_json). Compare to ground truth via fuzzy matching for synonyms and tolerant numeric comparisons.
Orchestration: implement job in airflow evaluation DAG; add lightweight pre-merge GitHub Action that runs a reduced sample when PR touches routing/config paths.
Storage: write run artifacts and samples to S3 path s3://redwood-evals/invocation-fuzz/ and metadata to eval-store. Record metrics to MetricsDB for dashboarding.
runbook: If regression_alert_count > 0: open INVESTIGATION ticket linking to the failing-run artifact and attach top 20 failing samples.
Triage flow: determine whether failure correlates with model change, runtime config, or kernel selection by checking recent commits and rollout logs.
If model change suspected: pin inbound requests to previous model_variant for impacted routes and notify SRE and product owners.
If runtime/config issue suspected: rollback config, run harness against candidate config, and add unit tests to cover discovered edge case.
Postmortem: add representative failing prompt to the eval corpus and create an automated guard in pre-merge check for future PRs.
comments: 2026-03-10 Sofia Patel: Initial ticket created after post-deploy spike where argument normalization errors increased for the payments-tool route. Decided we need stochastic samples beyond the current deterministic evals.

2026-03-11 Ethan Park: PoC implemented — extended eval-runner with a minimal fuzzer and ran 10k synthesized prompts. Early results show a 7% false-positive invocation rate on model-2026-02-3c. Will refine schema-fuzzer to reduce noise.
2026-03-12 Priya Nair (PM): Please include customer-impact mapping to each route so we can prioritize alerting. Also requested ability to suppress alerts during planned model rollouts.
2026-03-12 Review (Design): Suggest adding a small human-in-the-loop review for high-severity regressions to avoid noisy automated rollbacks — agreed; adding a 'review_required' flag to alerts.
Blockers: dependency on ENG-33904 for expanded eval-store APIs (artifact linking) — engineering dependency listed above.
